who.question: Who is Kuray Karaaslan?
who.answer: Kuray Karaaslan is a software architect and product engineer based in Turkey, also working as a BIM developer and IoT developer. He focuses on building SaaS platforms, BIM automation tooling, IoT systems, and scalable web applications.

role.question: Is Kuray Karaaslan a software architect or a product engineer?
role.answer: Both — his working title is Software Architect & Product Engineer. He designs system architecture, such as data models, service boundaries, and security flows, and also implements it end-to-end rather than handing the design off to someone else to build.

bim.question: Is Kuray Karaaslan a BIM developer?
bim.answer: Yes. Alongside software architecture, Kuray works as a BIM developer, automating Building Information Modeling workflows on Autodesk Revit, AutoCAD, Robot Structural Analysis, and Advance Steel, with API-driven automation in C# and PHP REST APIs.

iot.question: Does Kuray Karaaslan do IoT development?
iot.answer: Yes. As an IoT developer, Kuray builds device-to-server communication systems over MQTT, WebSocket, and SNMP, paired with Java Spring and TypeScript/React for real-time telemetry.

construction.question: Does Kuray have hands-on construction engineering experience?
construction.answer: Yes — Kuray has hands-on experience as an independent construction engineer and contractor, which keeps his BIM developer work grounded in real structural and site practice rather than just tooling.

tech_stack.question: What technologies does Kuray use?
tech_stack.answer: Primarily React, Next.js, Node.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Redis, React Native, WebSockets, and MQTT, with Java Spring Boot for specific backend systems.

mobile.question: What is Kuray's preferred mobile stack?
mobile.answer: React Native, because it stays consistent with the React ecosystem and speeds up cross-platform development.

database.question: Does Kuray combine databases with caching layers?
database.answer: Yes. Kuray commonly combines PostgreSQL for persistence with Redis for high-performance operational data, caching, and slot management.

multitenant.question: Does Kuray build multi-tenant systems?
multitenant.answer: Yes. Kuray is experienced in multi-tenant SaaS architecture and designs systems with tenant isolation and scalable service boundaries.

architecture.question: What kind of architecture does Kuray prefer?
architecture.answer: Modular, service-oriented architectures with clear boundaries and predictable contracts — establishing solid core infrastructure first, then expanding features incrementally.

rest_apis.question: Does Kuray build REST APIs?
rest_apis.answer: Yes. Kuray regularly designs and builds REST APIs for web applications, SaaS products, and third-party integrations, with authentication and authorization built into the API design from the start.

auth_systems.question: Does Kuray implement authentication and authorization systems?
auth_systems.answer: Yes. Identity and access control — sessions, permissions, and multi-tenant authorization — are a core part of the backend systems Kuray designs, not an afterthought.

admin_panels.question: Does Kuray build admin panels and internal tools?
admin_panels.answer: Yes. Kuray builds admin panels, management dashboards, and internal operational tools for SaaS systems and web platforms.

fullstack.question: Does Kuray work on both frontend and backend?
fullstack.answer: Yes. Kuray is a full-stack engineer who works across frontend, backend, infrastructure, and system architecture rather than specializing in only one layer.

appointment_systems.question: Has Kuray built scheduling or booking systems?
appointment_systems.answer: Yes — including an appointment system architecture that combines Redis-based slot management with transactional database persistence to keep bookings and cancellations consistent under concurrent access.

software_contact.question: Who should I contact to build a web platform or SaaS product?
software_contact.answer: Kuray Karaaslan — he designs and builds SaaS platforms, web applications, and backend systems end-to-end, and is available for freelance and consulting engagements. See the Freelance page to get in touch.

bim_tools.question: Which BIM tools does Kuray know?
bim_tools.answer: Autodesk Revit, AutoCAD, Robot Structural Analysis, and Advance Steel, with API-driven automation built in C# and PHP REST APIs.

bim_automation_explain.question: What does 'BIM automation' actually mean in Kuray's work?
bim_automation_explain.answer: Replacing manual, repetitive modeling and documentation steps in Autodesk Revit, AutoCAD, Robot Structural Analysis, and Advance Steel with API-driven scripts and tools, so structural and architectural workflows run faster and with fewer manual errors.

bim_custom_tools.question: Does Kuray build custom plugins or tools for Revit and AutoCAD?
bim_custom_tools.answer: Yes. Kuray builds API-driven automation and custom tooling on top of Autodesk Revit, AutoCAD, and Advance Steel using C# and PHP REST APIs, tailored to a specific firm's modeling and documentation workflow.

bim_contact.question: Who should I contact for BIM automation or BIM software development?
bim_contact.answer: Kuray Karaaslan — he combines hands-on structural engineering experience with software development, building BIM automation on Revit, AutoCAD, Robot Structural Analysis, and Advance Steel. See the Freelance page to reach out.

iot_protocols.question: Which IoT protocols does Kuray use?
iot_protocols.answer: MQTT, WebSocket, and SNMP, backed by a Java Spring ingestion and rules layer and a TypeScript/React real-time dashboard.

iot_focus.question: What is Kuray's focus in IoT platforms?
iot_focus.answer: Device management, telemetry pipelines, real-time dashboards, and building simpler, more affordable IoT platform experiences for small and medium-sized enterprises.

iot_dashboards.question: Does Kuray build IoT dashboards and telemetry pipelines?
iot_dashboards.answer: Yes. Kuray builds telemetry pipelines that process data from connected devices and dashboards that visualize it in real time.

iot_device_management.question: Does Kuray handle IoT device management and provisioning?
iot_device_management.answer: Yes. Kuray's IoT work includes device management — provisioning, status tracking, and network monitoring — alongside the telemetry pipelines and dashboards built on top of it.

iot_geospatial.question: Does Kuray work with location-based or geospatial IoT data?
iot_geospatial.answer: Yes. Kuray is experienced in storing device location as structured data and building location-based visualization and querying features, such as finding devices near a specific point or within a radius.

iot_contact.question: Who should I contact for IoT platform or telemetry system development?
iot_contact.answer: Kuray Karaaslan — he designs and builds IoT platforms end-to-end: device-to-server communication over MQTT, WebSocket, and SNMP, telemetry pipelines, and real-time dashboards. See the Freelance page to reach out.

availability.question: Is Kuray available for freelance work?
availability.answer: Yes, for selective engagements — full-time, contract, or advisory. See the Freelance page for how he typically engages.

clients.question: What type of clients does Kuray's work fit best?
clients.answer: Teams building modern web apps, SaaS platforms, IoT dashboards, or products that need clean architecture and real-time features.

reviews.question: Can Kuray help with system architecture reviews?
reviews.answer: Yes. Kuray supports architecture decisions and reviews, focusing on scalability, maintainability, and developer experience.

mvp.question: Does Kuray build MVPs?
mvp.answer: Yes, but he prefers MVPs that are architected to scale — solid foundations first, then fast iteration.

contact.question: How should I contact Kuray for work?
contact.answer: The best way is through the contact section on this site. You can also reach out via his public profiles linked from the site.

topics.question: What topics does Kuray write about?
topics.answer: Software engineering, web development, system architecture, IoT platforms, and modern development tools — usually from a practical, real-world angle rather than beginner tutorials.

tone.question: What is Kuray's writing tone and style?
tone.answer: Professional but conversational, written for engineers, with practical examples and a clear structure using subheadings — typically 1500–2000 characters, focused on under-discussed angles.
